neighbours.label: The slot where a high level or extreme degree is about to be named: 'to'/'into' right after a verb of rising, lifting or elevating (soared to, took the game to, elevated into), 'of' in praise like 'is of the highest', and the 'im-'/'in-' prefix opening an extreme word (immeasurably, inouïe). Weaker on sharp-change verbs like 'dropped'. Plain 'to' of motion or purpose (took them to the station) stays quiet.
neighbours.short: 'to' before a high level (soared to, took it to)
fire: The stock price soared to record highs after the earnings report.
Her brilliant passing took the game to another level entirely.
The new conductor elevated the orchestra into the very first rank of European ensembles.
This wine is of the highest quality, the best I have tasted in years.
The view from the summit was immeasurably beautiful.
Une beauté inouïe s'étendait devant nous.
Temperatures climbed to an unbearable forty-eight degrees by noon.
His second album lifted the band to international stardom.
quiet: Add two cups of flour and stir gently.
He moved the boxes into the garage before the rain.
The stock price stayed flat after the earnings report.
She took the kids to the park after lunch.
The new conductor moved the orchestra into the smaller hall for rehearsals.
This wine is from a small vineyard near the river.
The view from the summit was partly hidden by clouds.
Une maison simple s'étendait devant nous.

predictions: Blind test (label-only second author). Expect the rise/lift 'to' items to fire; the 'immeasurably' and 'inouïe' items are the risk.
notes: Step-in reader of bonsai1/L25/N8045+ (drop 0.84, the largest of the readers). Feeders-first arm: top feeders are L25/N8045+ (exceptional/remarkable intensifier) and L24/N4326+ (' to' setting up a stock verdict idiom). The output promotes measured degree words (significant, quite, clearly, notable); the + pole promotes extreme ones (impossible, utterly). Probes: the pole reads the left context only ('takes the game to' scores the same before 'the next level' and 'the store').
